DECISION: Fork @rlabs-inc/memory instead of using upstream (which has critical bugs and won't be fixed in time)
OPTIONS: Use upstream as-is / patch node_modules / build from scratch / fork
REASONING: node_modules patches get wiped on update; upstream curator is blind to existing memories causing massive duplication; manager LLM calls unreliable

SIX CHANGES IN FORK:
1. Curator gets existing memories context (buildExistingMemoriesContext) — fed into all curation paths so it can skip/supersede instead of duplicate
2. Global scope routing fixed — scope:'global' memories now route to storeGlobalMemory() not project store
3. Deterministic manager — no more LLM calls, 3 rules: >80% headline overlap→supersede, multiple state memories→keep newest, 3+ shared tags→link
4. event_date field added to schema for temporal anchoring of insights
5. supersedes field wired end-to-end (curator → parse → mark old as superseded)
6. Cross-segment dedup — accumulated headlines passed forward to subsequent segments

KNOWN BUGS TO FIX: superseded_by not set on project memories (only global); bracket stripping '[#id]' only strips '#'; Rule 3 linking increments counter but skips update

DEPLOYMENT: Old LaunchAgent still running rlabs version. After build, swap plist to point to fork binary.
